newsitem.title: USA: Detroit schools uncover new budget shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Detroit schools uncover new budget shortfall.

text.p: Detroit Public school officials have uncovered an approximately $20 million shortfall in the school system's previous year's budget, according to a school board spokesman and published reports.

Ken Coleman, spokesman for the school board, said Friday that the board was informed Tuesday of the budget shortfall and as a result has decided to reevaluate an annual review of school General Superintendent David Snead.
Coleman added that board president Irma Clark also ordered school officials to make the necessary cuts to bring the current budget into balance.
Because the school system is required to have a balanced budget the deficit from fiscal 1996 would have to be made up in the fiscal 1997 budget, Coleman explained.

According to a local newspaper report, the shortfall in the $1.4 billion fiscal 1996 budget, which was uncovered by an audit, comes on top of $79 million of cuts the school district undertook to balance its current budget.
Questions about the deficit were referred to William Aldridge, deputy superintendent of finance, who did not return phone calls.
The deficit revelation followed other problems at the school district, which has been trying to piece together how it spent proceeds from a 1986 bond issue.

Last month, school officials found 300 boxes of records that they hoped would contain that information. The lack of adequate accounting of the bond proceeds led Michigan Treasurer Doug Roberts to refuse to approve any further debt issuance by the school system under the state's school bond loan fund.
The Detroit schools had been reportedly planning a $124 million general obligation bond issue, the second such issue to tap into a $1.5 billion GO bonding program approved by voters in 1994.
